Maya: ran a quick perf pass on the AWQ weight-only build after the kernel selector change. seeing a 12-18% tail-latency regression for chat workloads that exercise long KV chains. attaching the micro-bench output below.

Maya: benchmark cmd: `./scripts/perf/run_kv_sweep.py --model redwood-ggm-slim --quant awq-int8 --groupsize 32 --batch 1..8 --prefix-cache true`

Maya: results snippet (median / p95 in ms per token)
```
groupsize=16 batch=1  median=2.3  p95=5.8
groupsize=32 batch=1  median=2.1  p95=6.9  <-- p95 regressed
groupsize=64 batch=1  median=2.0  p95=7.1
groupsize=32 batch=4  median=1.1  p95=3.4
```

Maya: odd bit is p95 increases at GS=32 even though median is fine. hypothesis: packing overhead + extra memcpy on the hot KV path is interacting poorly with new kernel selection (it picks the vectorized INT8 kernel more often, but the pre/post pack costs dominate for small batches).

Jorge: can you dump per-call breakdown? cpu memcpy vs kernel time vs batch-collector delay?

Maya: added `--profile=telemetry` and pushed a flame link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/1965432100 (short-lived)

Maya: flame shows spikes in `kv_pack_buffer` and `prepare_input_for_int8` before the kernel. kernel time slightly lower, but total end-to-end higher for GS=32 at low concurrency.

Anita: this matches what I saw in another workload where KV miss patterns create lots of micro-batches. batching heuristic currently triggers a flush if `current_prefix_len > 128` which can be hit by long chats, causing many small batches to reach the packing path.

Kai: aha. so two levers: (1) change heuristic to tolerate more in-flight requests (increase threshold/timeout) and (2) tweak packing implementation to avoid an extra copy for GS=32 when source is contiguous.

Jorge: short experiment idea: add fast-path that marks buffers as "no-copy" when quant codec returns contiguous layout. cheap check in `kv_pack_buffer` -> if true skip memcpy. should reduce p95 for small batches.

Maya: implemented no-copy fast-path in local patch and re-ran:
```
groupsize=32 batch=1  median=2.0  p95=4.2  (was 6.9)
```
Maya: p95 improved a lot. median stable.

perf-bot: perf regression alert cleared for 1965432100 after local fix (non-prod). rolling canary recommended. :white_check_mark:

Anita: we should also revisit kernel selection fallback threshold. right now it prefers the int8-packed kernel whenever expected token throughput > 500 toks/s, but with lots of KV overhead that estimate is too optimistic. maybe incorporate measured pre-kernel overhead into the decision.

Kai: agree. propose adding a small profiling window in the request pipeline that tracks average pre-kernel cost per route and factors that into kernel choice: effective_kernel_benefit = kernel_speedup - pre_kernel_overhead. if benefit < 0 choose alternative kernel.

Jorge: low-risk change: land the no-copy fast-path, run 24h canary across dedicated pools, collect per-route p95. then follow up with kernel decision calibration.

Maya: opened PR: https://git.redwood/eng/awq/patches/1324 (contains micro-bench + unit for contiguous buffer detection).

Anita: added to eng-ml board: TASK-4081 (investigate batching timeouts + fallback metric).

Kai: also flagging alert in runtime telemetry to capture # of pack memcpy calls per minute so we can detect if other models hit same problem.

Jorge: thanks, Maya. if canary looks good let's ship patch to prod and then iterate kernel selector.

Maya: will run canary tonight 00:30 PT and post results in this thread.

perf-bot: scheduled canary job 1965435800 -> will report back with aggregated stats.

Maya: quick note for postmortem if this regressed in mainline: root cause = packing-copy + optimistic kernel-selection that didn't account for pre-kernel cost; fix = no-copy fast-path + plan to make selector overhead-aware.

Kai: nice detective work. :mag:

Jorge: 👍
__notes: generated Slack thread for eng-ml about INT8 weight-only quant perf (AWQ/GPTQ) focusing on packing overhead, kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache behavior and profiling.
